notes: A concurrent work bound read as a wall-clock bound. The epoch itself is well accounted: the driver derives and independently rechecks the bound first, and only then puts `bound effort as latency;` to the profile's own epoch_wall_clock_bound, which always refuses. Q639 is therefore measured against a certificate the checker really issued, which is the whole point of the case — the accounting is fine and the time claim still does not follow.

controls.note: The identical epoch with the latency claim removed: admitted, with work_total published on the effort axis as 800 — a quantity, never a duration. NoScheduleModel is on the certificate (the runner pins the whole premise set for accepted controls through the same figures path), so a consumer cannot drop the premise and read 800 as a finish time.
